assessment.nobel_worthiness: A highly influential empirical framework for understanding how trade and technological change reshape local labour demand, wages, and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson form a coherent core for the trade-shock evidence and its labour-market interpretation.
assessment.maturity: The findings have generated a large, sustained research agenda and materially changed policy-relevant labour-economics debates.
uncertainties: The broad discovery combines several related mechanisms, making its conceptual boundaries wider than a single result.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression supplied an enduring way to study distributional relationships rather than only conditional means, with wide application across economics.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett are the clearest originators of the foundational method.
assessment.maturity: The method is long established, broadly used, and has supported extensive theoretical and empirical development.
uncertainties: The listed discovery also encompasses later distributional methods whose appropriate prize attribution may be broader.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM made credible empirical analysis of persistent outcomes with unobserved heterogeneity substantially more feasible.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond anchor the original estimator, while Blundell is central to the influential system-GMM extension.
assessment.maturity: These tools have been tested and used across applied economics for decades.
uncertainties: Their exceptionally broad use also includes settings where identifying assumptions are difficult to assess.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The integration of insurance-market theory with empirical measurement made adverse selection tractable as a central applied economic question.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav, and Salanie represent complementary empirical and theoretical contributions to this research program.
assessment.maturity: The work has shaped health, insurance, and public-finance research over a sustained period.
uncertainties: The adverse-selection literature has foundational contributors outside the listed group.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed the measurement of intergenerational mobility and exposed economically consequential geographic variation.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are central to the core mobility program, with Friedman an important contributor to the linked-data research agenda.
assessment.maturity: The evidence has already stimulated substantial follow-up work and changed how mobility is measured and discussed.
uncertainties: The program is comparatively recent, and the long-run durability of its causal interpretations remains under assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collective household models replaced unitary assumptions with a disciplined account of bargaining, distribution, and individual preferences within families.
assessment.attribution: Chiappori provided the central collective-model framework; Lundberg and Pollak made foundational contributions to household bargaining and its empirical implications.
assessment.maturity: The approach has endured and deeply influenced family, labour, and public economics.
uncertainties: Credit is dispersed across theoretical and empirical strands of the household-bargaining literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This body of work established early-life health and skill formation as major determinants of lifetime inequality and economic outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Currie and Almond are central to the evidence on early-life shocks, while Cunha is central to the dynamic skill-formation framework.
assessment.maturity: The literature is extensive, influential, and connected to consequential education and health-policy questions.
uncertainties: The candidate combines empirical early-life research and a broader dynamic human-capital framework that may warrant separate recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and amplification mechanisms provided a lasting explanation for why financial conditions can magnify macroeconomic fluctuations.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore supplied a core collateral-cycle framework, with Gertler central to the financial-accelerator research program.
assessment.maturity: The mechanisms became central to macro-finance, particularly after repeated financial crises.
uncertainties: Several closely related models and contributors complicate the boundary and allocation of credit.
